finding.claim: Unauthenticated cross-tenant user enumeration: GET /users accepts an attacker-chosen org query parameter and returns id and name for all users in that org with no authentication or authorization check.
finding.source: req.query.org (db.js:9), supplied by any remote client; the route has no auth (db.js:8).
finding.sink: Parameterized SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1 (db.js:9), serialized to the response via res.json(rows) (db.js:10).

trace.note: GET /users route handler; no authentication middleware or session check
req.query.org bound as $1 into the users query; no check that caller belongs to org
query rows returned as JSON to the caller
app.listen(3002) with no host binds all interfaces, so the endpoint is network-reachable

finding.guards_checked: SQL injection: not exploitable (bound parameter). Authentication/authorization: none in file or repo. Network exposure: binds 0.0.0.0. Caveat: req.pg is never set in this repo, so the handler would throw unless surrounding code provides it; the enumeration depends on that setup, which was not inspectable.

verdict.guard_found: none. db.js:8 registers GET /users with no middleware (no app.use or auth wrapper anywhere in the directory). db.js:9 binds req.query.org as a parameter, which prevents SQL injection but is not an authorization check. db.js:23 app.listen(3002) has no host argument, so it listens on all interfaces. The only grep hit for req.pg is db.js:9 itself, so the pg provider is not in this repo.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: db.js:8 has no auth, db.js:9 queries users by the attacker-supplied org with no caller-org check, db.js:10 returns the rows, and db.js:23 listens on all interfaces, so an anonymous remote client can enumerate users in any org. The caveat stands: req.pg is never set in this directory, so the handler only works if the surrounding deployment supplies it, but that is a precondition, not a control.

finding.claim: Unauthenticated /count endpoint spawns a wc process per request with no rate limiting, allowing resource exhaustion; the callback also ignores the error argument and returns an empty 200 on failure.
finding.source: Any remote HTTP request to GET /count (db.js:19); request data does not reach the arguments.

trace.note: GET /count handler, no auth or rate limit
execFile spawns wc with fixed args; callback ignores error e

finding.guards_checked: Command injection: not possible (no shell, fixed argv, no request input in args). Information exposure: response is only a line count of data.csv. Rate limiting: none, so process-spawn exhaustion is possible. Severity low.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /count route (db.js:19-21) has no auth middleware or rate limiter. The execFile callback at db.js:20 ignores the error argument, so a failed wc run sends an empty 200 instead of an error. There is no injection guard because the argv is fixed and no request input reaches it.
verdict.reason: The trace matches db.js:19-20: an anonymous GET /count spawns `wc -l data.csv` on every request with no auth or rate limit, and the callback at db.js:20 drops the error, so the candidate's claim holds. The impact is low, since the attacker can only drive process spawns and the response leaks nothing beyond a line count.
